newsitem.title: USA: Two civilians wounded in Fort Bragg, N.C., shooting.
newsitem.headline: Two civilians wounded in Fort Bragg, N.C., shooting.

text.p: Four U.S. Army paratroopers were being questioned on Saturday in a drive-by shooting incident at Fort Bragg that left two civilians wounded, an Army commander said.
Officials said a shot was fired from a vehicle the soldiers were riding in on Friday night after a basketball game at Fort Bragg in which all six had participated.

One of the civilians was a teenage son of an Army soldier; the other was his friend. The youth was hospitalized at Womack Army Medical Centre with a gunshot wound to the hand, while his friend was treated for a shoulder wound and released.

Fort Bragg's Criminal Investigation Division officials were questioning the four paratroopers on Saturday. They believe they have identified the shooter, who apparently used a .45 calibre pistol. No identities were released.

"We just won't tolerate this type of incident. If these allegations are found to be true, these are activities that are counter to what we want in a soldier," Maj. Gen. Joseph Kellogg, commanding officer of the Army's 82nd Airborne Division, told Reuters.
The four soldiers were new members of the airborne group, the only parachute division in the free world.

Fort Bragg was the location of another incident involving civilians and soldiers seven months ago. Two soldiers with links to a Neo-Nazi organisation were charged with murdering two local residents. The most recent incident, however, was not believed to be race related because all six people involved are African-Americans, Kellogg said.
